## Carried from #19247 (duplicate of this card, filed by the `domain:cli` seat out of #18431 review flag H)

#19247 is the same defect as this one and has been taken off the dispatch queue. Three things it recorded that this card does not — carried here so nothing is lost when it closes.

### 1. Both readers agree; only the fixture disagrees

| reader | depth it walks |
|:--|:--|
| the #18428 uncollected-directory **warning** | `src/PKG/docs/` |
| the #18431 per-package **collector** | `src/PKG/docs/` |
| ⚠️ the in-repo ADR-0130 fixture | **`src/packages/PKG/`** |

⭐ That framing matters for the decision below: this is **not** two readers disagreeing about a convention. The two readers agree. The reference fixture is the outlier — which is exactly why "whose depth is wrong" is a real question and not a bug report.

### 2. ⛔ Moving the fixture is not the fix

**#14122 / the hotcrm split** is what settles which depth the convention means. So the likely remedy is *"read both depths, or warn at the deeper one"*. Renaming the fixture's directories to match today's walk would make the symptom vanish while leaving the convention unstated — ⛔ it hides the question rather than answering it, and the next fixture reintroduces it.

### 3. Blast radius is measured at zero

The fixture ships no docs today, so nothing in-repo is currently being dropped. PR #18962's `## Acceptance notes` records this. ⇒ this is a **card**, ⛔ not a rider on a PR, and there is no urgency argument for settling it quickly or badly.

### ⚠️ Why this card is not being dispatched

Both cards say the same thing and it bears stating plainly: **the first act here is a convention decision, not an edit.** Which depth ADR-0130 means is not something a dev can settle from the code — the code implements one reading, the reference fixture embodies the other, and picking either changes which directories the build claims to understand. Dispatching a dev at it would make them guess a ruling.

⇒ Routing it as a decision rather than a task.

**Ruled: `os build` derives each package's docs directory from the packages the artifact registers, not from a fixed depth under `src/`.** A (declare `src/<pkg>/docs/` the convention and rename the reference fixture) hides the question and re-arms it on the next fixture; C (scan two levels) is a second magic number. Under B both layouts in this repo — the flat `src/<pkg>/docs/` and the ADR-0130 D4 fixture's `src/packages/<pkg>/docs/` — are collected, the `docs/uncollected-directory` warning covers Markdown under any registered package that the collector did not take, and a single-package stack's behaviour is unchanged by construction (its one package resolves to the same directory as today).

**Execution:** `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in this stroke; `domain:cli` seat dispatches, `priority:p2` unchanged. The dispatch names: `packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts` (`uncollectedDocsDirectories` and the collector, resolved per registered package), one test per layout (the flat one and `examples/app-multi-package`'s), the single-package regression pin, a `@objectstack/cli` changeset; the dev's first reading is whether `packages[]` is assembled before the collector runs (if not, the resolution point moves to where it is — report, ⛔ do not restructure the build). #19247's carried notes on this card stand.

## Claim — `domain:cli` execution PM seat #6024 · dispatching on maintainer ruling B

The maintainer ruled this card (batch #204 item 5, letter **B**, relayed by the director seat at `5754492000`) and the execution line moved it to `pm:queue`. Dispatching now.

```text
Claim: PM loop round 87
Session: `session_01QCdUBjM47SxioST9z5Zwdf`
Branch: `claude/issue-18965-docs-dir-resolves-per-registered-package`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-18965`
Domain: `domain:cli`
Seat: `domain:cli#1`
File surface: `packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts` + tests + a `@objectstack/cli` changeset — the set the ruling itself names. ⚠️ A fence, not a prediction.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — quoted from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts`, derived in a detached worktree at `32b5831c4e`: *"no path-derived mandate … the tier stays the PM's per-card judgment call (floor sonnet · default opus · ceiling fable)."* Judged DEFAULT.
Clause-②: ⚠️ **state it yourself, with your reason.** This widens what `os build` collects, so it is not obviously `no`. ⛔ This seat is not asserting it for you. On the at-tier question the gate is explicit and this lane is not covered: a contract-review-tier review is *"owed in the spec and skills lanes … default-tier build"* — this is `domain:cli`, so the build is default-tier and the review is in-seat.
Labels you may write: **`skip-changeset`, and only if your own measurement refuses a changeset** (⛔ it should not — the ruling names one). ⛔ Every other label stays this seat's.
```

## The ruling, in its own words

> **Ruled: `os build` derives each package's docs directory from the packages the artifact registers, not from a fixed depth under `src/`.** A (declare `src/<pkg>/docs/` the convention and rename the reference fixture) hides the question and re-arms it on the next fixture; C (scan two levels) is a second magic number.

⛔ **The fence it preserves, from batch #147 item 4 (`5715694492` on #18431): a single-package stack's behaviour must not move.** The ruling says this holds "by construction — its one package resolves to the same directory as today." If your implementation cannot keep that by construction, that is a finding: say so before you make it true by special-casing.

The ruling also names the first thing to read: **is `packages[]` assembled before the collector runs?** If it is not, the resolution point moves to wherever it is — ⛔ **report that, do not restructure the build.** ⛔ This seat has deliberately not pre-answered it.

## ⛔ The card's code quote is STALE — this seat's own landing moved it

⚠️ The card locates the defect at **`uncollectedDocsDirectories`**, and triage praised that as symbol-anchored rather than line-anchored. **That symbol no longer exists** — 0 hits across `packages/cli/src/` at `origin/main` `32b5831c4e`, against a lit control (`collectDocsFromSrc`, 2 hits in that file). `df0c856e01` (PR #18962, card #18431) — **landed by this seat earlier in this same shift** — replaced it. The quoted `for (const entry of packageDirs)` block is the pre-#18962 file.

Re-derived, the live shape:

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts:395` `sweepPackageDocsDirectories(srcDir, refs)`** — the sweep. It reads `fs.readdirSync(srcDir)`, then for each **direct child** builds `path.join(srcDir, entry.name, COLLECTED_DOCS_DIR)`. ⇒ **the fixed one-level depth is still there**; what #18962 added is *ownership* — matching that directory name against `ref.directoryNames` — not *resolution*.
- **`:365` `docsPackageRefs(packages)`** — the artifact's `packages[]` reduced to what a docs directory can name. This is the input the ruling's "packages the artifact registers" means.
- **`:309` `uncollectedDocsMessage(rel, files)`** — and ⭐ **its own docblock at `:298-307` already anticipates this ruling**: it says the warning is kept, "not removed and not weakened", for a *narrowed* set — a stack with **no `packages[]` at all**, and a directory matching **no package or more than one**. The `refs.length === 0` branch implementing that is already in the file. Read it before changing anything: part of your job may already be done, and the honest outcome is to say which part.
- ⚠️ **`:310`'s message still reads "package docs are read from `src/docs/` only (ADR-0046 §3.2)".** Under B that sentence becomes false for the stacks B newly covers. The docblock above it argues it stays exactly true for the `refs.length === 0` case. ⇒ decide, with the docblock's reasoning in front of you, whether the string needs to change; ⛔ do not change it reflexively and ⛔ do not leave it wrong.

## ⚠️ The fixture the ruling names has NO docs directory, and never did

Measured at `32b5831c4e`: `examples/app-multi-package/` contains exactly **7 files** — `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `objectstack.config.ts`, `package.json`, `src/packages/core/index.ts`, `src/packages/orders/index.ts`, `tsconfig.json`. No `docs/` anywhere. `git log --diff-filter=AD` over `examples/app-multi-package/**/docs/**` returns nothing, so none was ever added or deleted.

⭐ **Lit control**: `examples/` holds 256 files, of which **11** sit under a `/docs/` path (`app-showcase`, `app-todo`, all at the flat `src/docs/`). So the probe can see docs directories under `examples/` — it found none in this fixture.

⇒ the card is right and precise: it never claims the fixture *has* a dropped doc; it states the failure as a **repro** over the fixture's *shape*. But the ruling's "one test per layout … and `examples/app-multi-package`'s" therefore needs a decision from you: **add a docs directory to the reference fixture, or build the two-level layout inside the test's own fixture.** Say which you chose and why. ⚠️ Editing a reference fixture that ADR-0130 D4 points at is a change with its own readers — weigh that, don't just do it.

## Pins

1. The two-level layout (`src/packages/<pkg>/docs/`) is collected and attributed to the right package.
2. The flat layout (`src/<pkg>/docs/`) is collected exactly as today. ⭐ **This is the lit control** — without it, pin 1 is satisfied by a collector that grabs everything.
3. ⛔ **The single-package regression pin the ruling demands**: a stack with no `packages[]` behaves byte-for-byte as today, warning text included.
4. A directory matching **no** package, and one matching **more than one** — both keep their current, distinct answers.

## ⭐ Escape, and it is real

If your reading shows B cannot be built where the ruling assumes — most likely because `packages[]` is not assembled before the collector runs — **report it and land nothing** rather than restructure the build to make the ruling fit. That is the ruling's own instruction, not this seat softening it. **Eight orders from this seat were wrong this shift and a dev caught every one; one of them cited a precedent for the opposite of what it did.** Push back.

## ⛔ Why this correction exists — the seat got the protocol backwards

The claim at `5754811161` wrote prose into the `Clause-②` field — *"state it yourself, with your reason"* — trying to hand the judgement to the dev. `check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19492` refused it at **exit 4**, and its reason is the part worth keeping:

> A missing reading is NOT a declared `no`: one of those is a decision and the other is an absent one … ⛔ Do not fill the line in on the claiming seat's behalf; **the declaration IS the judgement.**

⇒ **the claiming seat must declare; the dev measures and reports.** Leaving the field open was not humility, it was a missing decision wearing humility's clothes, and it left the enqueue gate's content limb with nothing to read. **Order error #9 this shift**, and a fresh kind: the previous eight put a *wrong* value in an order; this one put *no value* where the protocol requires one.

## The declaration, and it is the seat's own reading

**`yes`.** `os build` will collect package docs from layouts it previously ignored — a two-level `src/packages/<pkg>/docs/` under the ADR-0130 D4 shape. Artifacts that build clean today gain `docs[]` entries they did not have. That is a **widening of the accept set**, and clause ② is directional: widening triggers it; pulling a door back to a contract it already declared does not. (That direction is exactly why #19417's install-door card declared `no (narrowing)` while this one declares `yes` — the two cards sit on opposite sides of the same test.)

⚠️ The dev's report reached `yes` independently and stated the same directional reason. This seat re-derived it rather than adopting it: ADR-0046 anchors collection at `src/docs`, and nothing in the declared contract already promised the deeper layout — so this is new acceptance, not enforcement of an existing promise.

## ⛔ And the label fence was wrong again, in the shape of error #7

The dispatch order narrowed the dev's label budget to `skip-changeset` alone. But it *also* asked the dev to determine clause ②, whose `yes` answer requires the **`needs:contract-review` dual carrier** — a label the same order forbade. That is **order error #7 recurring**: a prohibition not checked against the acts the order's own success requires. Fixing it once for `skip-changeset` and not generalising is the actual failure.

⇒ the carrier is this seat's to hang, and it is being hung on **both** limbs (this card and PR #19492) in the same stroke as this correction. ⛔ The dev wrote no label and was right not to.

## On the review this owes

The tier gate for this surface is explicit that a contract-review-tier review is *"owed in the spec and skills lanes … default-tier build"*. This is `domain:cli`, so the build is default-tier and the review of record is in-seat — ⛔ not a reason to skip it, and ⛔ not a reason to commission an at-tier subagent that the lane rule does not call for. The carrier comes off only against that recorded review, on the head it judged.

## Answering the round's open question — and correcting this seat's own correction

The round flagged a tension it declined to resolve, correctly: `check-clause2-carriers.mjs`'s `c6NoReviewOfRecord` docblock says *"a cleared `yes` OUTSIDE them is a limb hit on another lane's card, and the remedy is lane **ROUTING** … ⛔ never a default-tier self-review"*, while this seat's correction at the clause-② declaration said the review of record is **in-seat** here.

Its recommendation was **A — read the gate rather than either prose.** That is the right instinct and it is what settles this.

### What the gate actually answers

`node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19492` → **exit 0**, with the carriers hung on both limbs and **no C6 row printed at all**. `reviewOfRecord` reads `not-owed` for this pair, so C6 returns nothing.

And the rule's own landing commit says it in its subject, which is not a docblock and cannot be read two ways:

```
e15870f7a0  2026-09-18T23:51:43Z
skills(pm-dispatch): key the clause-② contract review by lane —
  spec and skills owe it on every round, OTHER LANES OWE NONE (#18903)
```

`laneOwesReview`'s own text agrees: *"The lane rule owes the review at tier on EVERY round those two lanes deliver, `yes` or `no` — 「交付后复核只 spec 与 skills 车道欠，每轮达档」."*

⇒ **`domain:cli` owes no contract review of record — not at tier, and not in-seat.**

### ⛔ So this seat's correction overstated, and that is order error #10

The clause-② correction comment said the review *"is in-seat — ⛔ not a reason to skip it"*. The accurate statement is that **this lane owes none**. Same family as error #8 this shift: a rule asserted from a partial reading instead of read from the instrument. ⚠️ The difference from #8 is direction — #8 demanded work a precedent forbade; this one demanded work the lane does not owe. Both are the seat inventing an obligation.

⭐ What the round did with it is the part worth keeping: it **flagged the tension and chose no side**, because landing is the PM's act. That is exactly right, and it is why the error cost nothing.

### On the precedent the round cited

It named PR #18962 / card #18431 — same lane, same file, same seat — as a `Clause-②: yes` that landed. ⚠️ Read rather than recalled: that pair **did** get full in-seat `## Contract review of record` comments (`5747212041`, `5747574143`, two FAIL rounds). But `e15870f7a0` landed **2026-09-18T23:51Z** and those reviews were written **2026-09-20T03:04Z** — *after*. ⇒ that seat did **more** than the lane rule required. Not wrong, not a precedent that obliges this round, and ⛔ not evidence the rule says otherwise.

### What happens next on this pair

⛔ Nothing is cleared yet, and the carrier stays hung: CI has not converged on the current head `4afa1e4669` (17 complete, 14 running, **no red**), and `TypeScript Type Check` — the check that failed on the **superseded** head `097806adc4` before the round's second push — **has not reported on the current head yet**. A failure naming a dead head is not this head's state, and ⛔ a head that has not been measured is not green.

When it converges green: a provenance comment citing this reading and the head, the dual carrier stripped in one stroke, `--pair 19492` re-run as the **post-strip** gate, then ready and arm.

## ⛔ Landing is BLOCKED on a conflict only the maintainer can settle — and this seat has been wrong on this rule twice tonight

PR #19492 is complete and green (all three CI layers, `TypeScript Type Check` included, at head `4afa1e4669`). It is **not landable**, and the reason is not the code.

### What happened, stated against me

This seat cleared the dual `needs:contract-review` carrier on the strength of a **pre-strip** reading of `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` — exit 0, no C6 row — and concluded the lane owed no record. The **post-strip** run, which is the one this seat's own protocol calls the gate, answers **exit 4**:

> C6 — … this pair's card sits OUTSIDE the spec and skills lanes (`domain:cli`), so a `Clause-②: yes` there is a **limb hit**: limb-hit work is the spec lane's, whichever seat found it, and the clear this pair made **stands on nothing this lane can produce**. … Remedy — **lane ROUTING, ⛔ not a self-review** … ⛔ This lane neither writes a default-tier record nor spawns the at-tier subagent.

⇒ the carrier has been **restored on both limbs** (gate back to exit 0, pair correctly not-landable). **Seat error #11 this shift**, and the third on this one rule: #10 was inventing an in-seat obligation; this is reasoning from the pre-strip state after writing down that the post-strip exit is the gate. ⭐ The round that built this flagged exactly this tension and **declined to choose a side** because landing is the PM's act. It was right, twice.

### The conflict, measured

| authority | what it says |
| --- | --- |
| **the maintainer's ruling** (batch #204 item 5, `5754492000`) | *"`domain:cli` seat dispatches, `priority:p2` unchanged"* — this card is this lane's |
| **the gate** (`c6NoReviewOfRecord`, landed `e15870f7a0` 2026-09-18) | a `Clause-②: yes` outside spec/skills is a limb hit; the remedy is **re-laning to `domain:spec`** or splitting the contract work there |

Both cannot be satisfied by this seat.

### Three measurements that bear on it

1. **This PR touches `packages/spec` zero times** — 3 files total: a changeset, a new test, and `packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts` (⭐ control: 3 files in the diff, 0 of them under `packages/spec/`). The remedy's own scope line reads 「新 `packages/spec` 工作恒由 `domain:spec` 收口」 — *new `packages/spec` work*. Re-laning would hand the spec lane a PR with nothing in its surface to review.
2. **There is no conforming precedent, and the non-conforming one is this seat's.** PR #18962 / card #18431 — same lane, same file, `Clause-②: yes` — was cleared against **in-seat** `## Contract review of record` comments (`5747212041`, `5747574143`) on 2026-09-20. `e15870f7a0` landed **2026-09-18T23:51Z**, before that. ⇒ that landing did what this lane may not do. ⛔ Recorded as a fact about a merged pair, not offered as cover for this one.
3. **Direction, not surface, is what the clause turns on** in the adjacent case: #19417 narrowed a published wire accept set from `packages/runtime` — no `packages/spec` file — and declared `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. By the same reading, this card **widens** what `os build` accepts, so `yes` is the honest declaration, and the limb hit follows from it.
